2. Briefly stated, petitioner is a company engaged in rendering services of Food Business Operator,
engaged in the business of manufacturing, processing, distribution, sale of food.

Respondent no.1 is also engaged in the business of owning and operating an online market place located at URL www.snapdeal.com, the mobile website located at m.snapdeal.command mobile application under the name & style of 'Snapdeal' which acts as an online/ electronic platform for seller and buyer.

20 . After having gone through the rival submissions of the counsels for parties and perusal of the record, I find that the petitioner has sought injunction U/Sec.9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
Petitioner, in order to succeed the relief of injunction, has to show three basic ingredients of it i.e. prima facie case, balance of convenience and irreparable loss.

Petitioner has brought on record the copy of agreement in question in order to show that there is written agreement between the parties with this effect that petitioner will provide food to the employees of respondent no.1.
The lockin period of the said agreement is stated to be of one year.

During the course of arguments,
counsels of both the parties have interpreted the terms & conditions of the said agreement in their favour.

Petitioner has claimed that agreement in question is not determinable whereas the respondent has claimed that the said agreement M/s. Deviram Restaurants Private Limited Vs.
Jasper Infotech Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. is determinable.

particularly from the agreement in question, it is apparent that petitioner has shown a prima facie case that he is in possession of the premises of the respondent no.1 for providing food to the employees of respondent no.1 for a fixed time.
However, there is a dispute between the parties as to whether the said agreement is determinable or not.
I am of the considered view that the said issue is in domain of the learned Arbitrator.

Moreover, the said termination will also destroy the reputation of petitioner which cannot be compensated in terms of money.

After having gone through the submissions of counsels for both the parties, I find that it is admitted fact that employees of the respondent no.1 are the main consumers of the petitioner and if the employees are having alleged complaints of food quality, then it is natural that they may not place the sufficient number of orders to petitioner for supplying food them.
In the said circumstances, there is no question of irreparable loss to the petitioner.

Further, if the petitioner would be able to prove before the learned Arbitrator that he has invested the huge money in the setting up of the food kitchen/ cafeteria to provide food to the employees of the respondent no.1 and respondent no.1 has breached the terms & conditions of the agreement in question, then definitely the petitioner would be compensated in terms of money by the learned Arbitrator.
28. With these observations, I am of the view that petitioner has failed to show two ingredients of injunction i.e. balance of convenience and irreparable M/s.

In the said circumstances, there is no question of irreparable loss to the petitioner.
Further, if the petitioner would be able to prove before the learned Arbitrator that he has invested the huge money in the setting up of the food kitchen/ cafeteria to provide food to the employees of the respondent no.1 and respondent no.1 has breached the terms & conditions of the agreement in question, then definitely the petitioner would be compensated in terms of money by the learned Arbitrator.
28. With these observations, I am of the view that petitioner has failed to show two ingredients of injunction i.e. balance of convenience and irreparable M/s.
